title: MW
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: As a boy, Michio Yuki survived a leak of the poison gas MW from a foreign military facility on a southern island; the leak killed the islanders and was covered up. Fifteen years later he is a banker who climbs through finance and politics by day and commits murders by night, aiming to obtain MW itself. Iwao Garai, the man who sheltered him that night and is now a Catholic priest, is drawn again and again into his crimes (Vertical blurb via AniList; Manga Bookshelf review).
life_message: A cautionary tale: state secrecy and weapons of mass death breed monsters, and a conscience that does not act becomes complicit.

content.note: Serial murders of women and children (publisher blurb); frequent, bloody killings and torture (review; AniList Torture).
Villain-protagonist thriller, mass death on the island, dark ambience (blurb; MU Dark Ambience, Psychopath).

Rape, sexual abuse of a boy by an adult (later a priest), a sexual relationship between Yuki and Garai, bestiality referenced (blurb, review, MU Child Rape). Reviewer says the art is non-explicit, 'almost abstract'.
No drug use noted; the nerve gas is a weapon, not a substance (blurb).
Protagonist without conscience (blurb; MU Psychopath, Sadist); AniList lists a minor Suicide tag (to verify).
Disguise, impersonating victims, manipulation (blurb; MU Manipulative Protagonist).

dominant: Nihilism (critiqued); state power and cover-up; a priest's conscience

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yuki's revenge on those behind the cover-up is shown as monstrous, not honorable (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Neither state order nor lawless freedom is upheld; both fail (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Garai's private bond with Yuki versus duty to society (review).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Elites in finance and politics shown as corrupt (blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Church and Kabuki heritage both compromised (blurb, review).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Driven by survival of a poison disaster and its cover-up (blurb).

folkways.japan: Set in 1970s Japan with Kabuki family lineage and resentment over foreign military bases near Okinawa, reflecting postwar Japanese debates rather than a stated message.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer says deeper themes appear as story elements 'without much commentary'; reads as a caper (Manga Bookshelf).

personified.ideology: Religious conscience bound by guilt and the confessional seal

delivery.note: The book shows state secrecy and a compromised priest without lecturing; one review finds it shallow rather than preachy.

winners_losers: Yuki's schemes drive the plot and the officials who hid the leak are targeted; Garai's conflicted faith earns some sympathy but he is drawn into complicity.
